rule: GOAL: Catch the falling magenta block by positioning the blue bar beneath its path. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the blue bar; spacebar releases the block to fall. RULE: The bar acts as a temporary shelf; move it while the block rests to guide it into the correct notch. TRAP: Believing the block slides off automatically; it stays put until you move the bar and release it again.

GOAL: Match the four middle slots to the target color sequence shown at the top. CONTROLS: Click a palette color, then click a slot to move it there; click two slots to swap them; press Space to submit. RULE: Each move consumes one action from the limited counter, so direct placement is more efficient than swapping. TRAP: Assuming you must rearrange existing pieces by swapping wastes actions; simply moving colors from the palette to the correct slots is faster.

GOAL: Navigate from the start to the far corner using only two-cell jumps. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player exactly two spaces in the chosen direction, skipping the adjacent cell. RULE: You can only land on empty white squares; gray squares act as walls that block your landing. TRAP: Assuming you could stop at any clear square wastes turns; you must land precisely on your target or an intermediate white square.

GOAL: Align the yellow handle with the yellow marker in the black bar. CONTROLS: Clicking the blue area moved the handle horizontally toward the center. RULE: The walls moved in tandem, keeping the total height constant while shifting the handle. TRAP: Assuming the handle could move vertically into the bar, rather than just aligning horizontally.

GOAL: Guide the square to the planet by clicking within a short range. CONTROLS: Click near the square to move it toward the target. RULE: The square only moves if the click is within three steps of its current position. TRAP: Assuming you could click distant targets to pull the square across the map in one go.

GOAL: Align the plug with the socket by setting all horizontal and vertical indicators to black. CONTROLS: Click the top bar of a slot to toggle the horizontal state; click the bottom bar to toggle the vertical state. RULE: Setting every slot to the black-black combination moves the plug straight down into the target. TRAP: Assuming you must decode complex directional signals first; the simple uniform setting solved it immediately.

GOAL: Align the green handle with the bar by shifting white space between regions. CONTROLS: Click buttons above or below bars to transfer white pixels between adjacent regions. RULE: Pressing a button moves white from the region on that side into the neighboring region. TRAP: Assuming the button’s own region gains white; it actually loses white, requiring a non-zero source to function.

GOAL: Guide the sliding tip to the left end of the track. CONTROLS: Arrows move the tip four columns per press. RULE: Correct color patterns lock the mechanism, allowing further movement. TRAP: Believing you must match colors repeatedly instead of simply sliding the tip left.

GOAL: Arrange seven colored tokens into their correct hidden sequence using feedback from submissions. CONTROLS: Click two tokens to swap their positions; press space to submit the current arrangement. RULE: Correctly placed tokens stay put; incorrect ones flash to reveal their true target position. TRAP: Assuming the last submitted error flash indicates the next valid move rather than confirming the current failure state.

GOAL: Place seven letters into nested boxes to match the top row sequence. CONTROLS: Click a letter from the bottom palette, then click an empty slot in a box. Press space to submit. RULE: Read left to right; when hitting a colored port, fill that sub-box first before continuing the main box. TRAP: Treating the colored port outlines as empty slots to fill, rather than indicators for nested sub-boxes.

GOAL: Shrink the key tip to fit through the narrowed shaft and slide it into the handle. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the key; clicking the keypad shrinks the tip size. RULE: The key only fits when its width matches the gap, requiring a size change before sliding. TRAP: Assuming arrows alone could push the full-width tip through the tight charcoal constriction.

GOAL: Arrange colored blocks in sequence to match target positions, using a special port piece to link two separate boxes. CONTROLS: Click a piece in the palette, then click a slot in a box to place it. Press space to confirm the arrangement. RULE: The port piece determines how the two boxes combine into a single reading order, fixing the position of pre-placed items. TRAP: Assuming the port can go anywhere; it must sit in the specific slot that aligns the fixed item’s index with its target.

GOAL: Lower column E so the white block rests exactly on the yellow segment. CONTROLS: Click the button left of a bar to push liquid into the neighbor; click right to pull from the neighbor. RULE: Liquid cannot be pushed out of a column if doing so exposes the colored segment. TRAP: Assuming the cap prevents the receiver from overflowing, rather than protecting the donor’s submerged status.

GOAL: Arrange red blocks and blue blocks to match the target sequence. CONTROLS: Click a color to select it, then click a slot to place it. Press space to verify. RULE: The blue block sequence repeats to fill the gaps between red blocks. TRAP: Assuming red blocks separate distinct blue sequences, rather than one continuous pattern spanning the whole line.

GOAL: Place the left box into the empty left slot. CONTROLS: Arrows move the block; Space toggles a box's frame to attach or release it. RULE: A box attaches below the block when Space is pressed while facing it. TRAP: Moving the block before attaching causes it to slide past the target box.

GOAL: Rotate four glyph slots to match target colors using only three moves. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the selection cursor; pressing a direction cycled the selected glyph’s shape. RULE: Each slot held a specific shape; aligning all four shapes to their designated colors completed the level. TRAP: Assuming arrow presses moved the cursor instead of rotating the glyph caused wasted turns and confusion.

GOAL: Place three color ports in the top row to determine reading order, then fill bottom boxes to match the target sequence. CONTROLS: Click palette items to select, click slots to place, and spacebar to submit the solution. RULE: Each port sets the first slot of its matching box; subsequent slots follow that box's internal order. TRAP: Ignoring the pre-placed items in each box, assuming you must fill every slot from scratch.

GOAL: Reach the exit without touching the stationary guard. CONTROLS: Arrow keys slide you two cells per press. RULE: The guard kills you if you land on its square. TRAP: Assuming you must dodge its attack; it never moves, so just slide around it.

GOAL: Arrange colored items inside nested boxes to form a perfect palindrome pattern. CONTROLS: Click palette items to select them, click box slots to place them, press space to verify the solution. RULE: The sequence of items in each box must mirror itself exactly, creating a symmetrical visual pattern. TRAP: Believing ports can be placed anywhere; they must occupy specific slots to allow the correct color arrangement.

GOAL: Merge the bottom piece into the planet to trigger absorption. CONTROLS: Clicks moved the piece in straight, diagonal, or horizontal lines. RULE: Merging occurred automatically once the piece landed within six units of the target. TRAP: Assuming you needed to land exactly on the target center; getting close enough was sufficient.

ESTABLISHED: The beam pushes blocks right to position tip plus two, or pulls them left to tip minus four. It passes through a block only when that block is jammed against the right wall. FAILED: Extending the beam to reach the target slot pushes the middle block into the wall, blocking the final arrangement. GOAL IS NOT: Simply extending the beam to the far right wall to pass all blocks through. CONTROLS: Beam extends right to push blocks; retracts to pull attached blocks; left wall stops blocks; right wall allows pass-through.

GOAL: Align three paddles horizontally to clear vertical paths for upward-traveling copies. CONTROLS: Click selects a paddle; Left/Right arrows shift the selected one; Space launches the ball. RULE: Paddles split incoming objects, so you must move them out of the trajectory of rising copies to prevent crashes. TRAP: Assuming color changes or previous activations matter for physics; only the current position and selection state affect the outcome.

GOAL: Rotate seven sliding tiles to match their target symbols. CONTROLS: Arrows move the cursor; UP and DOWN rotate the selected tile. RULE: Tiles cycle through symbols in a fixed order, so you can calculate the shortest path to the goal. TRAP: Assuming all tiles cycle in the same direction or that you must press buttons sequentially for every tile rather than batching moves.

GOAL: Reach the exit while avoiding guards that charge along their facing lines. CONTROLS: Arrows move the player one tile in the chosen direction. RULE: Guards only trigger if you enter their line of sight or charge path, not just nearby. TRAP: Assuming guards react to proximity; standing still or moving parallel often avoids their charge.

GOAL: Align the plug’s red contact dot precisely with the center of the cross target. CONTROLS: Click extend buttons to lengthen plugs and move their contact dots toward targets. RULE: The dot must land exactly on the cross’s center point, not just touch the edge. TRAP: Assuming simple adjacency completes the level wastes time when precise alignment is required.

GOAL: Guide the beam to the pink socket. CONTROLS: Arrows move the light tip; code entry fires the beam. RULE: The beam teleports the tip to the target if aligned, ignoring walls. TRAP: Thinking the tip must physically squeeze through narrow gaps to reach the socket.

GOAL: Move each colored cross so its arms cover all matching dots. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active cross; Space switches between crosses. RULE: A dot is cleared only when a cross arm passes directly over it. TRAP: You cannot move both crosses at once; you must switch back and forth.

GOAL: Align blocks to direct falling copies into three specific top slots. CONTROLS: Click blocks to shift them; Space to trigger the cascade. RULE: Copies spawn beside the block and slide until hitting an obstacle. TRAP: Assuming copies vanish on collision; they actually stack, often blocking later paths.

GOAL: Reach the exit while dodging a bouncing orange enemy and a stationary red guard. CONTROLS: Arrows move your character two squares per step, occupying both intermediate and final cells. RULE: The orange bounces predictably; time your moves so your path never overlaps its current trajectory. TRAP: Assuming you can cross the guard’s line of sight without first destroying it by landing on its base.

GOAL: Position two beads so their midpoint aligns perfectly with the ring center. CONTROLS: Clicking an empty spot moves the white bead there; clicking a bead swaps its position with the white bead. RULE: The white bead always moves to the click location, making it the primary tool for precise placement. TRAP: Assuming you can move the green bead directly; you cannot, so you must maneuver the white bead around it to achieve the correct symmetry.

GOAL: Cover all colored dots by moving four shapes onto their matching targets. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected shape; Space switches between the cross, diamond, and other pieces. RULE: Shapes absorb dots only when perfectly aligned, reducing the pixel count of that color. TRAP: Assuming diagonal pixels connect; they do not, so each arm acts as a separate component.

GOAL: Align the yellow block with the fixed yellow bracket. CONTROLS: Click the red arrow to rotate the ring counter-clockwise. RULE: The yellow bracket indicates the exact target slot for completion. TRAP: Assuming the top bar counted down moves; it actually tracked total actions taken.

GOAL: Dock the block into the upper box after acquiring the key. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the block one step at a time. RULE: Collecting the cross unlocks the socket, allowing the block to enter. TRAP: Believing the box was a solid wall; it becomes passable only after taking the key.

GOAL: Reduce the board to a single remaining piece. CONTROLS: Click a piece to select it, then click a landing spot to jump over an adjacent piece. RULE: A valid move requires an adjacent piece and an empty hole directly beyond it. TRAP: Assuming the landed piece stays selected; you must click it again to choose the next jump.

GOAL: Match the highlighted panel’s ring to its thumbnail, interpreting colors as negatives. CONTROLS: Click ring cells to toggle their color between blue and red. RULE: Solved panels show thumbnails as color inversions of their current state. TRAP: Assuming the thumbnail displays the current state directly, ignoring the inversion logic.

GOAL: Arrange three moving shapes to cover all eight scattered dots at once. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the active shape; spacebar switches which shape is active. RULE: The level ends only when every dot is covered simultaneously in the final configuration. TRAP: Thinking dots are permanently absorbed when touched; they reappear if uncovered, requiring a single final layout.

GOAL: Match the grid to the thumbnails' hidden patterns by painting the correct cells orange. CONTROLS: Click a grid cell to change its color. RULE: White pixels in a thumbnail mean the corresponding neighbor cell on the main grid must be orange. TRAP: Assuming a direct image match failed; the rule is actually a negative or inverted mapping.

GOAL: Place both yellow blocks onto their matching brackets. CONTROLS: Click row buttons to rotate specific horizontal tracks; click outer arrows to cycle the perimeter. RULE: Rotations only affect blocks currently inside the active track, pushing them into adjacent cells. TRAP: Assuming blocks move globally regardless of position, wasting moves rotating empty sections instead of targeting occupied cells.

ESTABLISHED: The maze is a single black shape with no enclosed holes; all background connects to the bottom. The top-right bar correlates with elapsed time, not actions. FAILED: Moving blocks to top corners, aligning them, or assuming a hidden dark target. Treating the bar as a step counter. GOAL IS NOT: Reaching specific top cells, sealing the central column, or finding a hidden color variant. CONTROLS: Arrows move blocks; space waits. The timer bar grows independently of movement.

GOAL: Set the grid cells to the correct color. CONTROLS: Click a cell to switch its color between red and orange. RULE: A thumbnail’s white blocks match its center color; green blocks match the other color. TRAP: Assuming the thumbnail colors directly show the grid’s final colors, rather than acting as a legend relative to the thumbnail’s own center.

GOAL: Move the cross over the green area to recolor it, then position it to cover specific dots. CONTROLS: Arrow keys shift the cross; Space confirms actions. RULE: The cross’s arms regrow to full length whenever it moves away from the edge, undoing clipping. TRAP: Believing clipped arms stay short permanently, leading to panic about unreachable targets.

ESTABLISHED: A gray block spawns at your previous position after you leave it. FAILED: Waiting, moving in circles, and ignoring the timer did not stop the spawn. GOAL IS NOT: Avoiding the gray block entirely; it is an obstacle, not a failure state. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move; the timer ticks down with each step, triggering spawns.

GOAL: Guide the yellow and orange blocks to their matching target slots on the outer rings. CONTROLS: Click left or right side buttons to rotate the corresponding ring clockwise or counter-clockwise. RULE: Each click shifts all blocks on that specific ring by one position in the indicated direction. TRAP: Assuming shared intersection points move identically for both rings; they follow the unique path of the ring you activate.

ESTABLISHED: Vertical pushing works. Blocks move freely through the corridor to column 30. FAILED: Pushing a block into the wall at column 33; the block stops, and the wall does not move. GOAL IS NOT: Simply aligning blocks in the corridor or entering the right panel directly from the left. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the selected block; unselected blocks are pushed one space if the destination is free.

GOAL: Match a hidden color pattern so every thumbnail correctly shows which neighbors match its own color. CONTROLS: Click a cell to cycle its color; observe the small thumbnail images to deduce neighbor relationships. RULE: A white pixel means the neighbor shares the thumbnail's color; a gray pixel means it differs. TRAP: Assuming three colors make the solution ambiguous. The match/differ constraints fully determine the valid pattern.

GOAL: Move the box containing a cross to a specific spot next to another cross. CONTROLS: Click directions to move the box; click the box to trigger a jump. RULE: A cross in the box jumps over a stationary cross, capturing it and clearing the box. TRAP: Assuming the cross stays in the box after jumping; it actually leaves the box, emptying it to win.

GOAL: Guide the yellow block to the bottom-right bracket and the orange block to the right-side bracket. CONTROLS: Arrow buttons shift blocks along two hidden loops: horizontal arrows move blocks across rows, vertical arrows move them down columns. RULE: The loops are continuous; blocks exiting one edge of a line reappear on the opposite side of the connected line. TRAP: Assuming arrows only move blocks locally; they actually rotate the entire shared chain, affecting both colors simultaneously.

GOAL: Align the plug's red prongs with the distant sockets. CONTROLS: Arrows shift the entire piece three spaces per press. RULE: Move vertically first to avoid hitting walls, then horizontally. TRAP: Thinking you must press right immediately; vertical space was open and safe.

GOAL: Swap two blocks between opposite rooms. CONTROLS: Arrows moved one block; Tab switched blocks. RULE: Blocks pass only in wide corridors, never narrow chokepoints. TRAP: Believing blocks must stay in their starting rooms, ignoring wide upper bands for passing.

GOAL: Guide the black piece until its mirrored reflection covers the yellow target. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the black piece directly; the charcoal piece mirrors its movement across the vertical center line. RULE: The reflection flips horizontal positions but keeps vertical rows identical, so you must align both axes simultaneously. TRAP: Thinking the reflection follows the yellow shape’s orientation; it is strictly a horizontal flip of the black piece’s current state.

GOAL: Restore the grid to its target pattern by toggling lights. CONTROLS: Click cells to flip them. Press plus buttons to flip themselves and adjacent cells. RULE: Plus buttons affect neighbors, so plan presses before fixing single lights. TRAP: Assuming plus buttons only fix themselves; ignoring neighbor side effects causes extra clicks.

GOAL: Move two yellow blocks to the top corners by sliding them along a continuous path. CONTROLS: Top buttons shift blocks right along the top row; side buttons push blocks up the serpentine column. RULE: The path connects the bottom center to the top row, then wraps back to the bottom, creating a loop. TRAP: Assuming side buttons moved blocks down; they actually push blocks up the column toward the top row.

GOAL: Align the moving shadow exactly with the yellow target shape. CONTROLS: Arrows shift the active piece or mirror band; Space switches which one moves. RULE: The shadow mirrors the main piece across the band; move the band to position the mirror, then shift the piece vertically. TRAP: Assuming you can move the shadow directly wastes turns; you must manipulate the mirror axis instead.

ESTABLISHED: Red horizontal bar and blue bottom square are active. FAILED: Placing the green chip in the top-middle pit slot did not trigger a win. GOAL IS NOT: Simply connecting the wire to the chip in its current default position. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the green chip; specific keys toggle the red and blue connectors.

GOAL: Reach the center while avoiding moving hazards. CONTROLS: Arrows move one step. RULE: Hazards bounce off boundaries; time your arrival to dodge their paths. TRAP: Thinking hazards stop at edges; they reverse direction immediately, creating predictable loops you must wait out.

GOAL: Shrink the tip to a 2x2 block, navigate it to the corridor, and trigger the pink code to clear the path. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the block; clicks activated the pink code to destroy obstacles. RULE: Shrinking preserved the vertical color split within the new 2x2 area, allowing horizontal movement. TRAP: Assuming the split orientation would flip upon moving; the rule kept the vertical division stable for horizontal travel.

GOAL: Fill the top half white and the bottom half purple. CONTROLS: Click colors to select; Space stamps the pattern; arrows rotate the tool's angle. RULE: Rotating 180 degrees flips the stamp, painting the opposite half of the grid. TRAP: Thinking you must manually rotate back step-by-step; you can often reverse direction or reset instantly.

ESTABLISHED: The diver moves horizontally in six-unit steps and rises in water. The middle band ceiling is solid rock with no visible holes. The diver already collected the yellow item. FAILED: Moving horizontally within the middle and bottom water bodies did not clear the level. Probing for a ceiling gap yielded no results. GOAL IS NOT: Simply reaching the top of the middle band or collecting the yellow item. CONTROLS: LEFT and RIGHT move the diver horizontally by six units; the diver rises automatically in water.

GOAL: Move three shapes to matching color swatches. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected shape; Space cycles shapes. RULE: A shape takes the color of the swatch its center lands on, then must reach a matching dot. TRAP: Assuming shapes keep their original color; they change upon touching a swatch, requiring precise routing to avoid premature color shifts.

GOAL: Paint the square's bottom half white and its lower-right corner orange. CONTROLS: Arrows rotate the stamp; clicking a swatch selects paint; Space applies it to the grid. RULE: Rotating the stamp changes which grid region it covers, so align the pose before painting. TRAP: Assuming the stamp always paints the top-left corner wastes turns; check the active mask after rotating.

GOAL: Align three distinct shapes into a single connected cluster matching the target silhouette. CONTROLS: Click to select a piece; arrow keys slide it one cell in that direction. RULE: Pieces snap together only when their designated tip cells perfectly overlap with adjacent pieces. TRAP: Assuming a piece is settled once it looks close; verify every tip connects before moving on.

GOAL: Match each slot's shape to a specific target class by cycling through options. CONTROLS: Arrows move the cursor; UP and DOWN cycle the shape in the current slot. RULE: Shapes follow a fixed seven-state cycle; choosing the shortest path between current and target saves moves. TRAP: Assuming a simple six-shape loop ignores the hidden junk state, causing unnecessary extra presses.

GOAL: Guide the plug and band through the grid to complete the circuit. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the selected component; the spacebar cycles through components. RULE: Only the highlighted piece responds to arrows, so switch carefully to align parts. TRAP: Forgetting to verify the active piece causes wasted moves on the wrong component.

GOAL: Guide the band and two plugs to match a yellow target shape using limited moves. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected piece; Space cycles selection between the band, first plug, and second plug. RULE: Only one piece moves at a time; Space switches focus without moving anything. TRAP: Assuming pieces move together wastes moves; you must manually cycle selection to position each part separately.

GOAL: Match each slot's pattern to the target sequence. CONTROLS: Arrows cycle the current slot's glyph through a fixed rotation order. RULE: Identify the shared cycle order to calculate the shortest rotation distance for each slot. TRAP: Assuming the visible patterns form a simple linear sequence rather than a closed loop with hidden states.

GOAL: Align yellow markers to outer ring targets by adjusting their radial distance and angular position. CONTROLS: Right clicks increase radius, wrapping from max to min. Down clicks rotate position counter-clockwise. Middle click swaps inner and outer pairs simultaneously. RULE: Radial changes apply to the selected star’s spoke, while rotations shift the entire spoke’s orientation, requiring precise sequence to land markers on specific grid cells. TRAP: Assuming rotations affect only the current marker ignores that the whole spoke rotates, often misaligning other markers and forcing costly u

GOAL: Move two agents to opposite bottom chambers without crossing paths. CONTROLS: Arrows move both agents simultaneously in that direction. RULE: Agents stop if hitting a wall, allowing one to park while the other moves. TRAP: Assuming you must move agents to their final columns simultaneously; instead, park one against a wall to adjust the other’s position independently.

GOAL: Repaint the canvas to match the target pattern by layering shapes. CONTROLS: Click colors, use arrows to rotate the stamp angle, and press space to apply. RULE: Stamps paint entire regions based on their current rotation angle. TRAP: Assuming you can paint the final shape directly; you must paint a large overlapping area first, then cover the excess with the correct color.

GOAL: Deliver both required shapes to the two planets to clear the level. CONTROLS: Clicking moves pieces toward the cursor or merges nearby pieces into new shapes. RULE: The level completes only when every distinct shape shown in the header is placed on a planet. TRAP: Assuming shape placement order matters or that wrong pieces permanently block planets, causing unnecessary hesitation and wasted clicks.

GOAL: Connect all three bars end-to-end to form a single chain. CONTROLS: Arrows move pieces, SPACE rotates them, and clicking selects targets. RULE: A 180-degree rotation around the grid center maps opposite tips to their matching pairs. TRAP: Assuming rotation preserves position; you must re-align after spinning to close the loop.

GOAL: Place the first yellow token at the far right of the row and the second yellow token at the bottom-right of the square block. CONTROLS: Left and Right arrows shift the horizontal row and rotate the square. Up and Down arrows cycle tokens through the vertical column without affecting the square. RULE: Row and square movements are independent of column movements, allowing you to solve them separately without undoing progress. TRAP: Assuming vertical moves affect the square or horizontal moves affect the column wastes clicks; they are strictly independent systems.

GOAL: Fill the four quadrants with correct colors. CONTROLS: Mouse clicks rotate the view or select paint; Space applies paint to visible areas. RULE: Paint only covers the side facing the dock, requiring you to rotate to reach all sides. TRAP: Believing you could paint all sides from one angle wastes turns; you must rotate to access hidden faces.

GOAL: Move the vertical band, horizontal band, and plug to their target positions. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected object; Space cycles selection to the next object. RULE: Objects are selected in a fixed cycle, so pressing Space repeatedly changes which item you control. TRAP: Assuming the selection order matches visual layout or previous levels wastes actions on unnecessary Space presses.

GOAL: Connect four letter-shaped pieces into one continuous chain by matching their colored tips. CONTROLS: Click a piece to select it, use arrow keys to slide it, and press space to rotate it. RULE: Pieces connect only when their specific colored tips touch exactly, forming a single unbroken path. TRAP: Assuming you can fix alignment issues after rotating; rotating changes the piece's footprint, often creating new overlaps that block the final connection.

GOAL: Navigate the maze while evading moving orange blocks to reach the exit. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player one step per press. RULE: Orange blocks bounce off walls and pass through guard locations, revealing their true path only when not obscured. TRAP: Believing guards block orange blocks causes hesitation; they do not, so trust the bounce pattern over visual occlusion.

GOAL: Traverse the maze to the exit using minimal moves. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player one step. RULE: Gray cells are passable paths; black cells are solid walls. TRAP: Assuming gaps between blocks were walls when they were actually open gray corridors.

ESTABLISHED: The handle is in region B. The partner is fixed. The game logic is ambiguous regarding whether ropes can pass through obstacles or if only the handle's footprint matters. FAILED: Moving the handle to (30,10) was rejected as invalid, proving that Line-of-Sight is a strict constraint and ropes cannot cross obstacles. GOAL IS NOT: Simply placing the handle in a clear spot; the rope must also have a clear path to the partner. CONTROLS: Clicking moves the handle if both the handle's position and the rope's path to the partner are free of obstacles.

GOAL: Stack paddles so a falling beam splits into two paths hitting targets. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move selected paddle; space triggers the beam. RULE: Paddles only stop beams if they block the beam's exact column. TRAP: Thinking paddles block all paths; they only stop the specific column they occupy.

GOAL: Paint the grid with four overlapping diagonal color zones. CONTROLS: Arrows rotate the painter; clicks select colors or stamp the pattern. RULE: Stamp order matters: later colors only overwrite cells within their specific zone. TRAP: Rotating the wrong way adds moves; always check both directions for the shortest path.

GOAL: Match the color and shape of top tiles to the bottom row using minimal moves. CONTROLS: Arrows move the cursor; UP cycles the tile's glyph state. RULE: Only the glyph class matters, not the exact rotation or pose. TRAP: Assuming precise pose matching is required wastes time on unnecessary clicks.

GOAL: Align three floating shapes onto a central crosshair to complete a symmetric pattern. CONTROLS: Arrow keys shift the currently selected shape; mouse clicks select a new shape. RULE: Each shape must be centered on the vertical or horizontal axis to trigger its reflection. TRAP: Assuming the band stays fixed; it moves with the selection, requiring you to re-center after every click.

GOAL: Place beads so their midpoint lands exactly on target shapes. CONTROLS: Click an anchor to grab it; click a target spot to drop it. RULE: A bead snaps to the nearest valid anchor; the midpoint must hit the shape’s center. TRAP: Thinking any free spot works; if the midpoint misses the shape, the move fails.

GOAL: Align each color group’s centroid to its target location to clear the board. CONTROLS: Click a bead to select it, then click an empty spot to move it or another bead to swap positions. RULE: A group wins only when the average position of all its beads matches the target coordinate exactly. TRAP: Assuming beads block each other prevents valid moves; chains can overlap freely, so ignore visual collisions when planning paths.

GOAL: Rotate the logo by covering specific points to unlock the final door. CONTROLS: Arrows move the block; each move consumes energy that refills at yellow zones. RULE: Every third cover rotates the logo ninety degrees; three covers complete the shape. TRAP: Assuming a single visit to the pivot point counts as multiple covers; you must physically leave and return to register each turn.

GOAL: Navigate the blob to the right-side docking zone to finish the level. CONTROLS: Arrows move the blob; color codes trigger growth or teleportation. RULE: Growth anchors to the blob's bottom-right corner, extending left and up. TRAP: Assuming growth always extends downward, causing the enlarged blob to clip obstacles.

ESTABLISHED: Room one holds five crosses with a hard minimum of two; room two has two crosses; the right room has one. Two boxes exist, one inaccessible from its side. FAILED: Reducing room one to a single cross, assuming standard room-clearing rules apply like previous levels. GOAL IS NOT: Clearing every room to zero or one cross, as the geometry makes this impossible in room one. CONTROLS: Movement shifts crosses between adjacent open cells; pushing into walls or boxes blocks movement entirely.

ESTABLISHED: Yellow panel extends right at col 42; green panel extends right at col 57. Left glyphs retract panels. FAILED: Clicking yellow panel at col 39 was a dead click with no animation or state change. GOAL IS NOT: Simply clicking anywhere on the yellow panel to extend it, as arbitrary positions fail. CONTROLS: Mouse clicks on specific glyph centers (col 42 for yellow, col 57 for green) trigger extensions; left-side glyphs trigger retractions.

GOAL: Extend the yellow and green bars to their target lengths within nine moves. CONTROLS: Clicking the left glyph retracts a bar; clicking the right glyph extends it. RULE: Only the precise center of each glyph registers as a valid input. TRAP: Assuming the entire bar area is clickable wastes moves on dead inputs.

ESTABLISHED: The notch-up mechanism is confirmed. Horizontal wrapping is unproven but suspected. FAILED: Attempts to mate the plug with the socket via standard positioning failed due to parity and size mismatches. GOAL IS NOT: Mating the plug inside the socket's fixed bar region. CONTROLS: Clicking grid cells sets movement (Left) or rotation. Running executes the sequence.

GOAL: Lift the plug four units into the socket. CONTROLS: Click grid marks to toggle instructions; click Run to execute. RULE: Each column’s vertical mark pattern acts as a barcode encoding a single movement command. TRAP: Assuming marks operate independently; they form a combined code, so extra marks cancel the move.

GOAL: Rotate the letter shapes to align their tips with the yellow beam. CONTROLS: Click a letter to select it, use arrows to move it, and press space to rotate. RULE: A letter is solved only when its tips touch the yellow beam, turning gray. TRAP: Selecting a covered letter fails; click its exposed edge instead.

GOAL: Guide the bead to the target centroid by moving it step-by-step. CONTROLS: Click empty space to move one step. Click another bead to swap positions. RULE: The group's center must land on the glowing marker to win. TRAP: Thinking you can jump far; each click only moves the bead to an adjacent empty cell.

GOAL: Route the plug through a wall gap to seat it perfectly in the socket. CONTROLS: Click grid cells to toggle horizontal or vertical path markers. RULE: The plug’s notch must align exactly with the socket’s bump to connect. TRAP: Assuming any path through the gap works; only the precise alignment fits the geometry.

GOAL: Slide the block through the wall into the socket. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected block; clicks select a block. RULE: A block slides up to five squares until hitting a wall or another block. TRAP: Assuming walls are solid barriers; they actually allow sliding blocks to pass through completely.

ESTABLISHED: Pressing specific coordinates shifts water between adjacent columns by three units. Alternating two distinct presses restores the initial water distribution. FAILED: Holding the valve open by maintaining equal water levels does not cause water to flow through or dissolve the plug. GOAL IS NOT: Activating the yellow plug by matching water levels in its adjacent columns, as this requires an impossible height. CONTROLS: Clicking coordinates transfers three units of water from one column to its neighbor, altering surface heights instantly.

GOAL: Move the floating marker into the second tank and raise it to the target height. CONTROLS: Click transfer buttons to move water between adjacent tanks; click the orange plug to let the marker pass through. RULE: The marker only rises with the water level, so keep the target tank filled while moving the plug. TRAP: Assuming water flows freely once the plug opens; it does not, requiring manual pumping from neighboring tanks.

GOAL: Clear a path for the diver to rise from the lower pool to the upper pool and reach the target marker. CONTROLS: Click blocks to destroy them; use arrow keys to move the diver horizontally. RULE: Destroying a block in the ceiling and the floor directly beneath it creates a vertical shaft for immediate ascent. TRAP: Assuming you must clear the entire width of the rock band; you only need one narrow column aligned with your horizontal position.

ESTABLISHED: Merging two small pieces creates one larger piece; the goal is delivering a large yellow piece to the planet. FAILED: Moving pieces directly into the moving ring causes them to vanish; attempting to cross the ring's lane while it is present fails. GOAL IS NOT: Delivering a small piece or a non-yellow piece to the planet. CONTROLS: Clicking a cell moves a selected piece toward it; clicking an empty distant cell burns a turn without moving.

GOAL: Guide a shrinking plug through a maze into a matching socket. CONTROLS: Click grid marks to set column actions: shrink, shift left, or move down. RULE: Combining specific vertical and horizontal marks triggers precise single-step movements or size reductions. TRAP: Assuming all moves are uniform; ignoring that the plug must shrink before navigating tight vertical gaps.

ESTABLISHED: The trough is 10x6. Five boxes and one orange exist. Boxes chase the player; the orange chases boxes. FAILED: Attempting to fill all slots or trap the orange by blocking paths has not worked. Range-based actions on distant boxes failed. GOAL IS NOT: Filling all six slots or simply placing five boxes. CONTROLS: Movement shifts position. Space toggles adjacent box states or attaches white boxes; it does not affect distant boxes.

GOAL: Route a character through a timed grid to reach the exit before energy runs out. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the character one step in the chosen direction. RULE: Yellow pads instantly refill your energy meter to full, allowing long, safe detours. TRAP: Assuming every refill is necessary wastes actions; skipping a nearby pad often yields a shorter, optimal path.

GOAL: Place a block to hold the tail, retracting the head to open the corridor. CONTROLS: Arrows move; Space toggles modes and places or removes blocks. RULE: Pressing Space in Mode A places a block at your current location. TRAP: Pressing Space in Mode B removes blocks instead of placing them.

GOAL: Reach the exit by navigating around a snake while managing a conditional block. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player; Space rewinds time to reset the level state. RULE: A block only materializes when you move at least two cells away from its location. TRAP: Believing the block appears instantly; it stays hidden until you create sufficient distance.

GOAL: Align the moving block's shape with the fixed green target zone. CONTROLS: Arrows shift the block; clicks rotate it to fit. RULE: The block fits only when its silhouette exactly covers the green area. TRAP: Assuming rotation is optional; overlooking orientation mismatch caused failed alignments.

GOAL: Guide the chip to the yellow pit. CONTROLS: Arrows move the chip; toggles rotate the red arm or shift the blue square. RULE: The rotating arm acts as a bridge only when aligned vertically, creating a path upward through the obstacle. TRAP: Assuming the blue square is static; it must be toggled to the top slot to cover the gap before climbing.
